papers.title: Climate change drives northward range shifts in invasive forest pests and pathogens
papers.authors: Haoran Wu, Gu Jiqi, Chengzhang Zheng, Yadvinder Singh Malhi, Cecilia A. L. Dahlsjö
papers.abstract: Abstract Invasive tree pests and pathogens are increasingly threatening forests worldwide. Understanding how a warming climate and changing precipitation patterns will affect the future distribution ranges of these pathogenic species requires systematic analysis across a variety of host trees and pathogenic species. We analysed 31 major tree pests and pathogens that have caused widespread and extensive damage globally, predicting their current and future distribution under various climate change scenarios using species distribution modelling. Our results showed that tree pests and pathogens will consistently shift northward, threatening northern temperate and boreal forests between the years 2041 and 2080. On the other hand, some warmer regions, including southern Europe, were expected to experience fewer pest and pathogen outbreaks in the future. Annual mean temperature, mean temperature of the warmest quarter, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and precipitation of the driest month contributed to the species distribution models, indicating that warming temperatures and moderate precipitation may promote the survival, reproduction, and spread of the pathogenic agents. papers.title: Plant disease detection and recognition using hyperspectral remotely sensed data: A review
papers.authors: Subramanian Vishalini, Ramalingam Kumaraperumal, Ramasamy Jagadeeswaran, Karuppusamy Sivasubramanian, Kavitha Saravanakumar
papers.abstract: Plant diseases are an inevitable challenge in agricultural production, yet timely intervention and effective management practices can significantly prevent crop losses and sustain yield and quality. Conventional diagnostic approaches depend on visual evaluation and labour-intensive, time-consuming physical sample collection, making them inadequate for large-scale crop monitoring and often detecting diseases only after visible symptoms appear, considerably hampering the potential for early disease detection. These limitations necessitate unbiased and automated approaches to disease monitoring and diagnosis. By measuring spectral reflectance across hundreds of continuous wavelength bands in the visible, near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) domains, hyperspectral remote sensing represents a revolutionary technique facilitating non-invasive, spatially comprehensive crop health assessment. Disease-related physiological and metabolic changes such as chlorophyll loss, water stress and pigment alteration generate distinctive spectral signatures detectable by hyperspectral sensors with high resolution. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
papers.authors: Annie E. Prescott
papers.source: OpenAlex / Digital Commons - USU (Utah State University)
papers.abstract: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Insect-resistant rice and Metarhizium anisopliae sustain the brown planthopper susceptibility through AMPK-mediated lipid redistribution
papers.authors: Kai Lin, Yutao Hu, Guy Smagghe, Wenqing Zhang
papers.abstract: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens, rapidly overcomes host resistance and develops insecticide resistance, undermining sustainable rice pest control. Here, we show that combining insect-resistant rice IR36 with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae CQMa421 provides durable suppression of BPH under laboratory conditions. Across multiple generations, chemical insecticides drove resistance and host adaptation, whereas M. anisopliae maintained susceptibility. Combined exposure redistributed lipids by reducing diacylglycerol (DAG) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in the fat body and ovary while increasing DAG in the hemolymph, thereby prioritizing humoral immunity. This redistribution was mediated by AMPK activation in the fat body, which inhibited insulin signaling and lipid catabolism while limiting detoxification and reproduction. AMPK-mediated energy reallocation sustained BPH sensitivity to both resistant rice and fungal infection. Integrating plant resistance with microbial biocontrol therefore suppresses host adaptation and delays resistance evolution, offering a sustainable pest management strategy.

Frostbite: diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, and future directions
papers.authors: Noor Obaidi, Olivia A Agee, Irene Yau, Robert Moritz, Kristo Nuutila
papers.abstract: From cold-weather training to deployments in high altitude and arctic conditions, frostbite injury and its sequelae remain a serious concern in military operations. Frostbite harms tissue in two distinct ways. The first involves ice crystal formation within tissue, resulting in mechanical damage and ischemia. The second occurs secondary to the inflammatory and prothrombotic state caused by reperfusion from rewarming frozen tissue. Frostbite injuries can be classified in a number of ways, but no perfect system exists. Initial work-up and diagnosis are primarily clinical. However, in equipped treatment facilities, advanced imaging modalities such as technetium- 99 m ( 99 mTc) bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance angiography, single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), and more can play a role in diagnosis and treatment. In resource-constrained environments, such as the deployed setting, management should involve an algorithmic approach. After concurrent hypothermia and/or trauma have been evaluated for and treated, active rewarming should take place so long as there is no risk of refreezing. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.authors: W. Kee Ng, Paulo Bártolo
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. papers.authors: Yue-Yang Zhuang, Jiamin Yan, Tie-Cheng Wu, Wen-shan Xu, Bao Jun Wu
papers.abstract: Background: Working memory deficits, one of the earliest hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease (AD), are closely linked to abnormal neural activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, has been shown to ameliorate early AD working memory deficits by modulating excitatory activity in the DLPFC, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Methods: This investigation was structured around 3 experimental phases. We initially applied tDCS to stimulate the left prefrontal cortex (PFC) of transgenic mice with 5 familial AD (5×FAD) 5 d per week for 4 weeks. Subsequently, we employed optogenetic (Opt) techniques to modulate left PFC glutamatergic neurons. Finally, we inhibited soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment receptor (SNARE) expression in the left PFC to elucidate the essential function of SNARE complex assembly with chaperone molecules in orchestrating synaptic vesicle release. papers.authors: Viviana Mosca
papers.source: OpenAlex / Nova Science Publishers (Nova Science Publishers, Inc.)
papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. One of the principal pathological hallmarks of ALS is the abnormal cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein involved in RNA metabolism and stress granule dynamics. Mutations in the TARDBP gene have been associated with both familial and sporadic ALS and are thought to contribute to altered cellular stress responses, defective RNA processing, and impaired proteostasis. papers.title: Abiotic and biotic stresses affecting honey bees: A review
papers.authors: Mohammad Ilyas Motmayen
papers.source: OpenAlex / Aureviaj Journal of Natural Sciences
papers.abstract: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) are indispensable pollinators that underpin global food production and biodiversity, yet their colonies face unprecedented challenges from a complex web of environmental and anthropogenic stressors. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the major biotic and abiotic threats undermining honey bee health, emphasizing the interactive and cumulative effects that often prove more damaging than individual stressors acting alone. The ectoparasitic mite Varroa destructor, in concert with vectored viruses particularly Deformed Wing Virus (DWV) emerges as the most devastating biotic threat, forming a mutualistic symbiosis that perpetuates escalating immunosuppression and colony decline. Beyond parasites, pathogens including Nosema ceranae, bacterial diseases and fungal infections, alongside large predators such as the predatory wasps, pose significant challenges. papers.title: Mycoparasitism of Podosphaera fragariae by an Ampelomyces strain under greenhouse and growth chamber conditions
papers.authors: Yuma Ibuki, Ayano Aisaka, Márk Z. Németh, Yuto Morisha, Miyu Fujita
papers.abstract: We investigated the mycoparasitism of an Ampelomyces strain on a strawberry powdery mildew (PM) isolate using electrostatic and digital microscopic techniques. Spores of the Japanese Ampelomyces strain Xs-q were spray-inoculated onto 10-day-old colonies of Podosphaera fragariae (Japanese isolate KSP-7 N) formed on either the adaxial (upper) or abaxial (lower) surfaces of strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duchesne ex Rozier) leaves under greenhouse and growth chamber conditions. Conidia from P. fragariae KSP-7 N colonies were collected using an electrostatic insulator plate and quantified with a digital microscope. No conidia were attracted from Xs-q-inoculated colonies under either condition. Microscopic monitoring revealed distinct infection processes. Under our greenhouse conditions, Ampelomyces strain Xs-q collapsed KSP-7 N conidiophores within 8–9 days post-inoculation (dpi) without pycnidia formation inside the PM mycelium. Under our growth chamber conditions, mature Ampelomyces pycnidia developed within conidiophore foot cells at 11–12 dpi, regardless of leaf surface. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). papers.abstract: Guantánamo Bay has been a symbol of alleged human rights violations and indefinite detention for over two decades.Located on the island of Cuba, the naval base has been operated by the United States since 1903, and following the 9/11 terrorist attacks, it was designated to be a detention facility for the suspected terrorists captured in the War on Terror.The present doctoral dissertation examines two types of image construction related to Guantánamo: constructing the image of the enemy and constructing the image of the self.The dissertation explores the discrepancies and overlaps between the macro-narrative constructed by the U.S. government between 2001 and 2024 and the micro-narrative of former detainee Mansoor Adayfi.Through the analysis of presidential rhetoric and legislative measures, the dissertation investigates the deliberate processes of enemy-image construction (enmification) of Guantánamo detainees by the administrations of George W. Bush, Barack Obama, Joseph R.Biden, and Donald J. Trump.In parallel, it examines the systematic deconstruction of Adayfi's sense of self through practices of mortification and enhanced interrogation, as well as the subsequent reconstruction

papers.title: Pathophysiology-guided biomarkers and therapeutics for precision trauma medicine in polytrauma with musculoskeletal injuries
papers.authors: Rex Jeya Rajkumar Samdavid Thanapaul, Manoj Govindarajulu, Chetan Y. Pundkar, Peethambaran Arun
papers.abstract: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. To address this critical gap, we performed a comprehensive scoping review integrating evidence from basic science, translational studies, and clinical research published between January 2000 to June 2025, with particular emphasis on recent advances.
